title: Maintenance
summary: The Maintenance Worker's daily routine on the estate, the area protocols and the safety and quality standard.
body:
## 1. PURPOSE

To keep the estate facilities structurally sound, safe and beautifully presented through proactive repairs and careful care of the outdoor grounds.

## 2. SCOPE OF RESPONSIBILITY

- **Maintenance (all areas):** the Maintenance Worker is responsible for all repairs, lighting, plumbing checks, equipment servicing and the finish of walls and ceilings in every building and facility.
- **Cleaning (outdoor only):** the Maintenance Worker is responsible for keeping outdoor paving and hard surfaces clean. Indoor cleaning (mopping, dusting, vacuuming) is done by Housekeeping (see PEL-SOP-008).

## 3. DAILY ROUTINE

To make sure the estate is ready for residents and guests, follow this daily timeline and tick each task on the Daily Maintenance and Grounds Checklist (PEL-CHK-007):

### 3.1 Phase 1: first light inspection (07:30 to 08:30)

- **Safety check:** check the swimming pool gates, the children’s play area and the sports court fences for any hazards.
- **Full light check:** walk through the Library, offices, Function Hall, gym and Frail Care. Replace any blown bulbs immediately.
- **Plumbing check:** flush toilets and run taps in the public bathrooms and staff rooms to check for leaks or slow drainage.
- **Pools:** clean and treat the pools so they are ready for use for the day.

### 3.2 Phase 2: outdoor grounds and drainage (08:30 to 11:00)

- **Paving:** sweep all paving at Reception, the courtyard and the restaurant free of debris and cigarette butts.
- **Gulleys:** every morning, inspect all storm drains and gulleys and remove leaves, sand or plastic that could cause a blockage.
- **Lapa:** remove ash from the braai area and sweep the paving, hosing it down if stained.

### 3.3 Phase 3: repairs and structural maintenance (11:00 to 16:00)

- **The invisible repair rule:** when repairing chips or scuffs on walls, sand the area, fill where necessary and paint with the exact colour code from the Villa Del Mare Paint Log (PEL-REG-002). Never paint over dust.
- **Paint Log:** when a new paint is bought or a new colour is mixed, add it to the Paint Log with a photo of the tin label and a photo of the paint, and record the batch number.
- **Frail Care protocol:** knock and announce “Maintenance” before entering any of the 6 rooms. If a resident is resting or being treated, come back later.
- **Equipment checks:** do the daily checks on the gym machines, laundry equipment and pool pumps.

### 3.4 Tool return and fault log (16:00 to 16:30)

- **Tool check:** at 16:00 every day, clean all tools of dust and paint and return them to the maintenance store. Report missing tools immediately.
- **Fault log:** record every repair done during the day in the daily fault log. Report any major breakage you cannot fix to the General Manager with a photo and a list of parts needed.

## 4. SPECIFIC AREA PROTOCOLS

### 4.1 Drainage and gulleys

- **Rain protocol:** if rain is forecast, all other tasks come second. Check and clear every drainage point on the estate.
- **Kitchen gulleys:** every Friday, treat the restaurant and Frail Care kitchen gulleys as set out in PEL-SOP-010 Planned Preventative Maintenance (hot water and degreaser) to prevent fat-trap overflow.

### 4.2 Sports facilities

- **Astro care:** use the designated brush to keep the fibres upright on the soccer and bowls astro. Check for lifting seams weekly.
- **Courts:** check the net tension on the padel and tennis courts. Make sure gate latches are lubricated and close automatically.

### 4.3 Offices and co-working space

- Test all power points and make sure furniture is stable.
- Inspect walls for chair-back scuffs and repair them immediately.

## 5. HEALTH, SAFETY AND CONDUCT

- **Signage:** put out “Work in progress” or “Wet floor” signs whenever you pressure-wash paving or work on plumbing in public areas.
- **Chemicals:** keep all pool chemicals and maintenance solvents in the locked maintenance store.
- **PPE:** wear safety boots at all times, and gloves, goggles or a mask when the task requires it.
- **Professionalism:** wear the full maintenance uniform (see the Staff Handbook, section 7.2) and be polite to residents at all times, especially in the Frail Care wing.

## 6. MAINTENANCE QUALITY STANDARD

> **The gold standard:** “If a guest walks past, the estate should look like it was built yesterday.”

This means no flickering lights, no chipped paint, no sand on the paving and no slow-draining gulleys.

## 7. RELATED DOCUMENTS

- PEL-CHK-007 Daily Maintenance and Grounds Checklist
- PEL-REG-002 Villa Del Mare Paint Log
- PEL-SOP-010 Planned Preventative Maintenance
- PEL-SOP-008 Housekeeping
- PEL-POL-001 Staff Handbook (section 7.2, Uniform and appearance)
